audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows said Heimerdinger or Skill while every paragraph attached to them says Maokai wins. whys[1] through whys[6] describe him ignoring the nest, out-sustaining the beams and deleting you with one root; mid opens 'This is where Maokai owns me'; late says 'the straight matchup is lost' — yet win[1], win[2], win[5], win[6] read Heimerdinger and win[3], win[4] read Skill.
audit.why: packet.levelChart reads Skill at level 1 and Maokai for every row after, and the win rate is 44.44% over 126 games. The chart was the only part of the page claiming Heimerdinger wins anything past level 2, and diff/diffRating said EVEN 6/10 against the same evidence.
audit.corrected: phases[1..6].side + win[1..6] all -> Maokai as matched full+content pairs, ratings dropped to 3/10, every phases.why rewritten to state the real reason, and diff EVEN -> HARD with diffRating 6/10 -> 8/10, breakdown.difficulty, report[2] and report[14] brought along.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields call Heimerdinger's turret beams AD ('they're AD', 'every AD turret beam', 'your AD turret economy'), and four say Sap Magic heals Maokai every time he casts a spell or is hit.
audit.why: Heimerdinger's turrets deal magic damage — the AD claim would send a reader into completely wrong itemization reasoning. And Riot's Sap Magic text is precise: his BASIC ATTACK heals him on a moderate cooldown, and casting a spell or being struck by an enemy spell REDUCES THAT COOLDOWN. He is not healed by casting and not healed by your beams; your spells make the next heal arrive sooner. That still favours him in this lane, but for a different reason, and it is why anti-heal timing (report[8], already correct) matters rather than 'stop hitting him'.
audit.corrected: AD claims removed; Sap Magic restated as a cooldown-reduction heal on his attack in whys[2], spikes[3], mid and wants.foe[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere despite three sequencing cues in the packet.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1 and untargetable during the dash — that is both why nothing you throw stops it and why the 14s afterwards is the only window you own. Sapling Toss is 18s from 1100 range, Bramble Smash 7s, Nature's Grasp 130s from 3000 range.
audit.corrected: 14s, 18s/1100, 7s, 130s/3000 written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d, report[5], every rewritten phases.why, early, mid, whys[2], whys[4], whys[5] and spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire content layer is written in the FIRST PERSON — 'I have one turret', 'my turret beams', 'my immobile body', 'my job is'.
audit.why: Every other page in this champion speaks to the reader in second person. A page that narrates the author's own game reads as someone else's match, not as instructions the reader can act on.
audit.corrected: whys[0-6], early, mid, late and spikes[3] converted to second person alongside the substantive fixes.

edits.before: This is where Maokai owns me and there's no pretending otherwise. He facetanks my turret beams — they're AD and his Sap Magic passive heals him on every ability cast and every hit he takes — while his W ignores the zone and his Bramble Smash slows me off my own buildings. My one real card is the CH-3X center stun: if he W-roots in, I drop the grenade on his landing spot, W-rocket the burst, and walk before the Bramble Smash slow connects. At 6 his R Nature's Grasp roots me from offscreen with zero counterplay for an immobile champ, so I respect every missing-jungler timer like it's a death sentence — because it is.

Your one real card is the CH-3X center stun: when he W-roots in, drop the grenade on his LANDING spot, W-rocket the burst, and walk before the Bramble Smash slow connects. At 6 Nature's Grasp rolls in from 3000 range on a 130s timer with zero counterplay for a dashless champ, so treat every missing-jungler timer as a death sentence.

My job is to have cracked the map open with my push and vision before this point, because the straight matchup is lost.

notes: This page's chart was the opposite of its own prose. Every paragraph from level 2 onward says Maokai wins — mid literally opens 'This is where Maokai owns me' — while six of seven chart rows credited Heimerdinger or called it Skill, and the header said EVEN 6/10 against a 44.44% win rate. All six rows flipped as matched full+content pairs and the difficulty header brought with them. Two factual fixes: Heimerdinger's turret beams are MAGIC, not AD (stated three times), and Sap Magic heals off his BASIC ATTACK on a cooldown that his casts and your spell hits shorten — it does not heal him for casting or for being hit, which four fields claimed. The whole content layer was also written in the first person and is now in the reader's second person.
